D.treatment: Tabletop pulsed-laser and oscilloscope experiment with lecturer explanation

O.outcome_detail: Understanding the finiteness of light speed and that refractive material slows light

cells.quote: The concept of the experiment is easily grasped by non-science/engineering majors. Furthermore, the experimental output tends to lead to a good understanding of the finiteness of speed of light, which is otherwise not easy to experience directly.
cells.note: The authors report an institutional deployment with roughly 600 humanities and social-science students, but no comparison condition or formal outcome measure is reported.

D.treatment: Hands-on tabletop experiment using a pulsed laser, photodiode, and oscilloscope

O.outcome_detail: Students' ability to perform the experiment and obtain designed measurement accuracy

cells.quote: The experiments have been conducted essentially with no problems and the results are quite satisfactory.
cells.note: The study reports successful implementation and satisfactory results descriptively; it does not provide a comparator, formal performance assessment, or effect size.

D.treatment: First-time use of an oscilloscope within the tabletop experiment

O.outcome_detail: Student enjoyment and engagement with oscilloscope signal visualization

cells.quote: Most students seem to understand and enjoy the visualization of the signal provided by the oscilloscope.
cells.note: Enjoyment is reported impressionistically, without a comparison condition or formal measure.
